candidates.notes: Research candidate only; no verified legal public approach, parking or trail. Do not infer accessibility from geographic point.
candidates.sourceNotes: Regional 2026 Porcupine Mountains waterfall guide calls Bonanza/Greenwood Falls on Big Iron River, via M-64 and gravel access; independent waterfall photography resource reports a signed Greenwood Falls small parking area near Silver City. Validate landowner and legal entry, precise parking and seasonal road status. Village of Ontonagon business directory independently lists Bonanza Falls (Greenwoods) between Silver City and White Pine off M-64; NMU regional heritage guide gives one mile south of Silver City, west of M-64. These corroborate named destination and approach, but not legal parcel boundary or current gate. October 28 parcel-overlay review: MI GIS #124 intersects parcel recorded as Iron River Assoc., LLC, 03-113-001-00, while regional waterfall brochure coordinate intersects a different parcel recorded as Township of Carp Lake, 03-113-002-30, approx. 168 m distant. This is an ownership/access conflict requiring route-specific verification, not proof of trespass, closure, public easement, title, or safe parking. County states parcel GIS is not legal title evidence. Official 2025 Carp Lake Township minutes verify that township maintains Bonanza visitor signage, parking/turnaround, and facilities; Oct 2025 park closure planned for late month (weather-dependent), Dec 2025 confirmed closed until spring 2026. This establishes a seasonal municipal visitor location, not legal access to the adjacent privately attributed GIS falls coordinate. Current 2026 seasonal status unverified. 2026-10-28 official Carp Lake Township Parks & Facilities page explicitly labels Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) a park with falls and links a Google Maps destination at 46.8176942,-89.5674561. County parcel layer places this destination, sampled points on the westbound approach and regional brochure 46.817719,-89.570023 on township-attributed parcel 03-113-002-30. The natural falls GIS point remains on separately attributed nonmunicipal parcel. Local signed parking-to-upper-falls direct walk corroborated by Waterfalls of the Keweenaw; whitewater guide distinguishes two separate waterfall drops, so this guide explicitly excludes unverified lower-falls access. Neither municipal park listing nor parcel geometry authorizes unmarked downstream river travel; not an as-built surveyed trail.
candidates.outstandingGate: Visitor guide may describe signed township park lot and established upper-falls approach only. Current 2026 seasonal opening status is unknown; no public easement, drawn trail, parking waypoint or unrestricted access is established for separate GIS waterfall point #124 or lower riverbank.

candidates.name: Pemene Falls
candidates.landManager: Michigan and Wisconsin DNR, Menominee River State Recreation Area (public visitor approach on Wisconsin shore)
candidates.notes: Research candidate only; no verified legal public approach, parking or trail. Do not infer accessibility from geographic point.
candidates.sourceNotes: Wisconsin DNR: Pemene Falls hiking trail starts at end of Verheyen Lane off County Road Z; 0.5 mile to primitive overlook, shorter 0.8 mile loop and 1.9 mile loop. GIS falls coordinate requires independent reconciliation with official trail endpoint before promotion. Reviewed Pemene DNR official 2005 trail-map screenshot and 2018 park infrastructure map: Wisconsin lot + 0.5 mi designated overlook path, 0.8/1.9 mi loop options; separate Pemene Landing off Horseshoe Road is a boat access, not trailhead. Independent photographer Adam Martin geolocates the natural falls at 45.5941048,-87.777153, consistent with Michigan GIS #188 45.594123,-87.777192 (meters, not a route mismatch). Mapcarta Wisconsin named waterfall also 45.59413,-87.77734. Earlier 'GIS coordinate conflict' should be restated as DIFFERENT visitor overlook vs river feature, not evidence that the falls GIS coordinate is wrong. Current visitor road and seasonal access conditions not verified. Full admission gate resolved: Wisconsin DNR 2005 trail map shows southern Wisconsin Pemene Falls hiking trail lot, primitive 0.5-mi overlook and 0.8/1.9-mi loops, corroborated by DNR 2018 Pemene Falls Unit map. Official area navigation reference is 45.5884,-87.7847, not a measured lot. Natural state GIS feature #188 is at different location on the river. Pemene Landing boat access is NOT the hiking trailhead.
candidates.outstandingGate: Check actual current parking road/gate and posted park conditions before visiting. The GIS point is only the natural river feature, not a legal visitor parking or trailhead location.

locationReconciliation.conclusion: natural falls coordinate corroborated; official trail/overlook is a different point, not a contradictory map
locationReconciliation.trailhead: End of Verheyen Lane, off Wisconsin County Road Z

visitorRouteEvidence.routeScope: Wisconsin signed Pemene trail to primitive gorge overlook only
